scope: Three exact changed blobs and original receiver/transport/current call sites. Git API and pure V8 comparison only.

exact_replay.owner_tests: One unique old function body replaced; complete rest of file byte-identical.
exact_replay.evidence: Entire original 3928-byte production file preserved as prefix; appended helper is cfg(test).
exact_replay.support: One unique cfg(test) support re-export only.

findings.evidence: Helper calls the same private evidence_response(bytes, 1) and increments original_responses only after success. Only then does it receive the release message and return those exact original response bytes.
Joined original_responses must equal 1. Only original transport DeadlineElapsed/Closed/Unavailable are accepted; InvalidRequest, count zero, and a delivered successful reply cannot satisfy the test.

The unchanged evidence_client binds both original endpoints to 500 ms. EvidenceClient takes its only channel before I/O and restores it only after complete response/fresh verification. RootObservationStream also takes its stream and leaves it empty on timeout. The second legacy attempt is the same already-failed client and sends no new frame.

The command client used to attest actual C remains held. Before withdrawal its new independent readback returns a fully equal opaque completed receipt and exact attestation, after the same actual owner readback_remote and final authentication.

The original version.withdraw call remains. The same command then performs the physical post-withdrawal read and must return CommitUncertain. C owner bytes and source/Cell/control journal bytes are checked unchanged.

One existing original command channel performs exactly Execute, Readback CURRENT, and Readback withdrawal: server count3. One existing legacy channel records exactly one actual original response and no successful delivery; the second legacy call fails locally.

Only fixture-owned std thread joins move to spawn_blocking and are awaited, allowing the current-thread Tokio test reactor to continue driving the owner Handle.block_on I/O. No transport retry, longer timeout, forced cancellation, signal, or production runtime change is introduced.

The unchanged HostAuthorityPeerChannel checks its original deadline after the handler and before any response prefix. Errors consume/shutdown the same channel. The test helper does not bypass that code.

Source ordering proves successful actual owner response precedes the ACK gate. It does not establish that the owner response completes before the client's 500-ms deadline, nor that the gate alone causes timeout. A real owner read already longer than500ms remains possible; the exact new candidate still needs native execution.
